title: Usable release
goal: Open SIANN with one command or an installer and work in it as a Cubase user would: projects, audio import, arranging, transport, MixConsole, recording and plan review in place, in English, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese, proven by a scripted Cubase user's walkthrough (GitHub #83, criteria A to I of the UI redesign spec's section Usable release).
prerequisites: M5: every m5-ui-* feature is merged (phase 1 of the UI redesign) before any m5b-ui-* feature or m5b-cubase-walkthrough starts. The packaging, engine, bridge, parity and nightly features (m5b-package-windows, m5b-engine-*, m5b-bridge-*, m5b-protocol-parity, m5b-nightly-quality) do not build on the M5 UI and may start once M5's m5-ui-shell is merged. M5's own exit may still wait on the maintainer's reviews; M5b builds on the merged shell, not on the exit.
M2 (write-through recording and crash-safe takes, #21) and M4 (plugin hosting, registry and editors): merged.
docs/harness/follow-ups.md, section Before M6b, items 1 and 2: taken into m5b-engine-record. Items 3 to 6 stay before M6b.
M6a is not a prerequisite: nothing in criteria A to I needs automation.

humanGates.text: Install the unsigned Windows installer on a Windows machine that has no compiler, no Node and no SIANN checkout, start the app from the Start menu and play the demo session.
humanGates.how: The maintainer downloads the installer artifact of the package CI job, checks its SHA-256, accepts the SmartScreen notice for an unsigned build and records the result. humanGates.text: Record on a real audio interface: choose the input in Studio Setup, arm a track, monitor it, record with count-in and with punch at the locators, and judge monitoring latency and the placement of the take.
humanGates.how: The maintainer runs the installed build with the studio interface (ASIO and WASAPI) and a loopback cable or a microphone and click; CI proves the same paths on the fake device only. Needed for the exit check, not before the build.

humanGates.text: Review tour states 13 to 20 and 26 to 28 (ghosts and audition) in English, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese.
humanGates.how: The maintainer reads the PNGs per locale after m5b-ui-audition lands and lists required changes; fixes land before wave 6.

humanGates.how: Same procedure as M5's zh-glossary gate: the maintainer compares the additions to section 6.5 of the UI redesign spec with a Cubase running in Chinese and corrects the catalogs; needed before the exit check.

humanGates.how: The maintainer reads the tour artifacts of the package job (Windows) and of the siann-macos run; this is the last gate before the exit check.

humanGates.text: Approve the protocol shape of a request from the user to a connected agent: the method and MCP tool names, whether the agent polls or waits for its next request, the queue bounds, and what a request may carry besides its text.
humanGates.how: The plan phase of m5b-engine-agent-requests presents the shape with the threat it must not open (a request must never execute anything: a plan and its approval stay the only way into the session); the maintainer or the delegated reviewer decides before implementation.
humanGates.resolution: Decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-15: (1) delivery: the agent waits for its next request with an MCP tool next_request (long poll; the engine answers as soon as a request is queued, or empty after at most 30 s); (2) a request carries the user text plus context: the selected track and clip ids, the locators, the cursor position and the head revision (no audio); (3) bounds: at most 16 queued requests per connected agent and 4000 characters per text; a full queue is refused (agent_busy, shown in the UI); queued requests are not persisted and are dropped on engine restart. Text follows the display-text rules (no bidi controls, valid UTF-8).

humanGates.text: Approve the document change for the master gain (a singleton entity or a field on root).
humanGates.how: The plan phase of m5b-engine-master presents both shapes with the hashes and conflicts each implies; the maintainer or the delegated reviewer decides before implementation.
humanGates.resolution: Decided by the main session under the maintainer's delegation (Fable rule), 2026-11-15: a singleton entity master ({schema: siann.entity.master.v1, id: master, gainMilliDb}, ref master:master), present only while the gain is not 0 dB; master.set_gain 0 removes it and plan.preview shows before: null at 0 dB; the document stays siann.session_document.v2 (m5b-engine-buses-sends raises it later). Not a field on root, because root:root would conflict with rename and tempo plans; master:master fits the gesture leases unchanged; the entity diff picks a parameter set over a recompile; the master will grow mute and inserts; and E-1's locators are the precedent. Architecture spec, siann-model, Gestures and Master path.

features.title: One command and an unsigned Windows installer start the app with its engine
acceptance: At the repository root `npm run app` runs scripts/run-app.js (Node built-ins only; the root package stays dependency-free): it installs app/'s locked dependencies with `npm ci` when app/node_modules is missing or older than app/package-lock.json (compared through app/node_modules/.package-lock.json), always builds the app with `npm run build` (cheap, and there is no staleness stamp), finds the desktop-preset engine and configures and builds it through the preset steps scripts/check-all.js uses when it is missing, then starts Electron on it. `npm run app -- --plan` prints the steps without running them, and a unit test drives the planning function over a table of states (nothing built, app built, engine built, both, each on win32, darwin and linux); 'app built' means app/node_modules is present and not older than app/package-lock.json, so it only removes the `npm ci` step.

`npm run dist` in app/ uses electron-builder (a devDependency pinned to a release at least two weeks old, MIT; the Libraries table of the architecture spec names it, so no new ADR is needed) to write the NSIS installer SIANN-Setup-<version>-x64.exe and its win-unpacked directory, with the siann-engine.exe of the desktop-release preset (Release, JUCE, ASIO, statically linked MSVC runtime) where main.ts's engineExecutable() looks when app.isPackaged. Acceptance 1 is unchanged: `npm run app` keeps using the Debug desktop preset that scripts/check-all.js builds.

No signing step runs and no certificate, key or secret is read: the packaging configuration names no certificate, the CI job's environment holds no secret, and a unit test on the configuration fails when a signing field is added.

The package carries the licence texts: AGPL-3.0 for the package as a whole (ADR-0017), GPL-2.0 for SIANN's own sources, the JUCE and ASIO SDK notices, Electron's and Chromium's licence files and the OFL texts of the fonts; the installer's licence page shows the AGPL text. A test lists the unpacked directory and fails when one is missing.

A test reads the PE import tables of the packaged siann-engine.exe and of every DLL beside it and fails on an import that is neither in the package nor on an allow-list of Windows system DLLs, so the app needs no compiler runtime the user must install.

Playwright e2e against win-unpacked/SIANN.exe with SIANN_ENGINE_EXE unset, launched with SIANN_SHELL_TEST=1, SIANN_USER_DATA (an empty directory) and SIANN_ENGINE_TEST_ARGS=--device fake (main.ts reads these test hooks packaged or not; a hardening that removes them from packaged builds must change this test): the window opens, the renderer connects with the token handshake, the status bar's licence line reads AGPL-3.0-or-later with the build's commit, playback advances the playhead on the fake device, and quitting leaves no engine process.

CI: a Windows job `package` (pushes to main, workflow_dispatch, and pull requests whose paths the stepsForPath table of scripts/check-all.js maps to it; never for docs-only changes) builds the installer, runs the tests above, installs it silently (/S) into a temporary directory, repeats the smoke run on the installed app, uninstalls it silently, and uploads the installer with a SHA-256 file as a workflow artifact.

README.md gains a short section on running SIANN (public wording only): the installer, the SmartScreen notice of an unsigned build, and `npm run app` for a source checkout; docs/harness/runbook.md says how to build the installer locally.
Tour states changed: none.

features.title: Engine and protocol: create a session, import audio files as a job, media names (E-5 and the media half of E-4)
specRefs: siann-command (pure C++) — the core of SIANN
acceptance: session.create {path, name?} creates an empty bundle at an absolute path that does not exist (already_exists when it does; a UNC or relative path is invalid_params), rebinds the engine to it exactly as session.open does and answers {sessionId, revision}; its sample rate is the rate the output device runs at, 48000 with no device (Sample rate and media). Protocol tests cover the success, each refusal, and that the previous bundle's lock is released.

media.import {path, clientImportId} starts a job reported through job.status as render.start's is: it decodes a WAV or FLAC file, converts it offline to the session rate when it differs, writes the content-addressed media and its peak pyramid, and commits one media.add revision. The job's result carries the media id, and both hashes when it converted. A failed or cancelled import commits nothing and leaves no file under media/ (tests: unsupported format, truncated file, missing file, cancel during conversion). A repeated clientImportId answers with the first job, and importing content the session already holds answers the existing media id without a new revision.

The media entity gains an optional name (the imported file's base name, at most 255 UTF-8 bytes), set by media.add and by a new command media.rename (one revision, undoable). It is omitted from the canonical JSON when absent, so existing bundles and every recorded hash are unchanged (test on a literal earlier bundle). The renderer's read model, its fixture generator and the Node plan hasher accept the field.
The import does not hold the command thread: a transport.play sent while a ten-minute stereo file converts is answered before the job ends (test with a paced decoder on the fake device).

media.import and session.create are refused in the MCP propose scope and allowed in the trusted scope (they read and write paths on the user's disk); engine.capabilities lists both methods and features.mediaImport {formats: [wav, flac]}; docs/schemas documents them.
Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Engine and protocol: device inputs, track input, record arm, and recording into a committed take
acceptance: The engine process opens input channels: engine.devices reports inputChannels and outputChannels per device, engine.select_device {id, inputId?} opens an input (the same device, or another one where the backend allows it), and engine.status carries the open input's id, channel count and latency. With no input the record methods answer no_input and playback is unaffected.

A command track.set_input {trackId, input: {port, channels} | null} stores the track's input (an IoPort of Channels and I/O) as one undoable revision; the field is omitted from the canonical JSON when null, so earlier hashes hold. record.arm {trackId, armed} is engine state, not a revision (as cycle is): engine.status reports it, a record.changed event announces it to every connection, removing the track clears it, and a track without an input is refused with no_input.

transport.record {enabled: true} with at least one armed track starts playback and capture at the playhead; transport.record {enabled: false} or transport.stop commits exactly one revision holding a media.add and a clip.place per armed track (record.commit_take), placed by the record offset of the latency model: a loopback test on the fake device finds the recorded impulse within one sample of where it was played. session.undo removes the clips and media references and deletes no file.
While recording, record.changed carries per take {takeId, trackId, startFrame, durableFrames}, and the realtime channel carries the input meters of armed tracks, also while stopped.

An early end is unmissable (follow-ups, Before M6b, items 1 and 2): the take's result and its manifest carry endedBy (stop, overflow, disk or device) and overflows, record.changed repeats them, and what was captured before the end is still committed.

A kill during recording followed by a relaunch lists the pending takes in session.sync; record.recover_take {takeId, accept} commits one in the same revision shape or moves it to trash/, idempotently (engine launch test with the crash hook).
Recording with cycle on records straight through the right locator (the wrap is suspended while capturing); loop recording with one take per pass stays m6b-loop-takes.

engine.capabilities lists the methods and features.recording; MCP tools wrap record.arm and transport.record in the trusted scope only. The capture path adds no allocation, lock or blocking I/O on the audio thread (test linked with siann_rt_alloc_guard).
Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Plan review in place: the ghost model, and ghosts in the event display, MixConsole and Inspector (P2-1, P2-2)
acceptance: A pure function beside plans/describe.ts maps the plan's steps, its plan.preview result, the snapshot and the ticked steps to ghost descriptors for every change kind of section 4.2 (add track, place, move, trim and remove clip, remove track, gain, pan, mute, solo, rename, locators), each carrying its step number: one unit test per kind, and one showing that an unticked step contributes none. A ghost's values come from the preview's before with the ticked steps applied in order (as plans/step-rows.ts does), never from after wholesale; the step number is the 1-based index in the full plan; a cascade (the clips of a removed track) belongs to the step plans/entity-homes.ts homes it to when that step is ticked and on the same track, and otherwise to the track.remove (UI redesign 4.2); a ghost whose track exists neither in the snapshot nor through a ticked track.add is not produced (UI redesign 4.2). The locator ghost takes its new values from the session.set_locators step itself (left, right) and its before from the preview's locators:locators entity, since plans/entity-homes.ts homes no step to that entity. Each proposed track has ids of its own: the first track.add of a plan keeps the mockup's (track-ghost*, lane-ghost, strip-ghost*), and a later one takes ghost-2, ghost-3 and so on in step order, which the manifest's *ghost* rule still matches.

The event display draws them on its content layer (UI redesign 5.2) in the agent violet, dashed and hatched: a placed clip with its waveform, a moved or trimmed clip with the original at 38 %, as the mockup's draw(), and an arrow, a removed clip cross-hatched, an added track as a hatched lane with a dashed header, a locator change as a ghost band. The content layer is redrawn when the selected plan, its preview, its ticked steps or the ghosts toggle change; the hovered step's highlight is an outline on the overlay layer; a frame in which only the project cursor moved still does not redraw the content layer. Ghosts on the canvas appear at once: the 150 ms fade of UI redesign 1.6 applies to the DOM ghosts only (headers, strips, the Inspector), as a CSS transition that prefers-reduced-motion removes.

The MixConsole and the Inspector show a ghost cap joined to the real cap with both values, a violet tick on the pan control, a dashed ring on M or S, both names on a rename, and a dashed strip labelled as new, whose insert row (strip-ghost-inserts) stays an empty box, since a proposed track has no slots; the track header shows the gain readout with both values, the dashed ring on M or S (the mockup's .msr.ghost) and both names on a rename. A ghost the mockup has no markup for (the Inspector's volume and pan rows, both names on a rename, the dimmed strip of a removed track, the header's gain readout) is an added element styled in shell.css on the existing --ai* tokens (UI redesign 4.2).

Hovering a step outlines its ghosts and scrolls the event display and the MixConsole by the least amount that shows them. The target icon on a step row (the mockup's .go, which m5-ui-port-plans renders empty: this feature draws its icon and makes it a button) is the keyboard path to the same: it also shows the lower zone's MixConsole when the ghost is on a strip and it is hidden, and it pins the highlight until another step is located or the pointer enters another row; it sends no request. Clicking a ghost pins its step: the row is .hot with aria-current, the right zone opens on the Plans tab and the row scrolls into view. Unticking a step removes exactly its ghosts (e2e compares the test hook's ghost list with the ticked steps).

A pill in the toolbar names the overlaid plan and toggles ghosts, as does Ctrl+Alt+G; ghosts are drawn for the selected plan only and never for an applied, rejected or stale plan. Until m5b-ui-plan-metadata the pill and the Inspector's Agent changes section name a plan by its first step in user wording and "N steps", through one helper, which this feature extracts from the audition banner (plans/AuditionBanner.tsx builds that text inline today) and the banner then uses (UI redesign 4.3). With no reviewable plan selected the pill is not in the DOM and no box replaces it: it ends the toolbar, so nothing follows it (UI redesign 3.0), and no permanent empty-width token is added for it.
No protocol request is added: the e2e's request log holds plan.preview and what the Plans tab already sent.

Every new string is in the three catalogs. Tour states changed: 13 to 18 (ghosts and the pill; 17 and 18 select a plan that is neither applied, rejected nor stale, and 16, 19 and 20 show none), and the toolbar and the Inspector's Agent changes section in every state with a selected track; appends 26 (ghosts in the event display) and 27 (ghosts on the MixConsole). The Pool's state of m5-ui-port-toolbar took 26 on 2026-11-18, against the reservation of UI redesign, "Tour states": this pull request moves it from 26 to 31 (in app/test/e2e/ux-tour.spec.ts and in the m5-ui-port-toolbar row of docs/harness/test-matrix.md), the one exception to "appended, never renumbered" (UI redesign 7), and m5b-ui-media later turns state 31 into the Media tab's. Decided by Fable, delegated by the maintainer, 2026-11-18 (UI redesign 10.11, 8).

Ported from the mockup's markup (decided by the maintainer, 2026-11-17; UI redesign 10.9; docs/harness/agent-rules.md, "UI fidelity"): this feature's parts, *ghost*, proposal-pill, inspector-agent-changes, take the DOM structure, class names and data-part ids mockup.html gives them, are styled by the shared rules of app/renderer/ui and are wired to real data; a unit test holds the rendered structure to the mockup's markup and an e2e assertion finds each id in the window. Their gate in app/test/fidelity/manifest.json (m5b-ui-ghosts) goes from pending to report in this pull request and the --hold-* tokens of these parts are deleted; nothing sets a gate to enforce. A side-by-side screenshot of the app and the mockup is attached for each state this feature changes, in en and zh-TW, with the fidelity report; the maintainer reviews it by eye, and no geometry or pixel result blocks.

features.title: Engine: clip fade in and fade out (the fade half of E-9)
specRefs: siann-command (pure C++) — the core of SIANN
acceptance: A command clip.set_fade {clipId, fadeIn?: {length, curve}, fadeOut?: {length, curve}} (lengths in media frames as decimal strings, curve linear or equal_power) is one undoable revision; the two lengths together may not exceed the clip's length (invalid_fade), and a clip.trim that makes the clip shorter than its fades shortens them in the same revision. The fields are omitted from the canonical JSON when the length is 0, so existing hashes hold (test on a literal earlier bundle).

The clip player applies the fade gain per sample: the offline render of a faded clip equals a reference computed from the curve's formula within one LSB at 24 bit, and the realtime path nulls against the offline render, also after a locate into the middle of a fade and across a cycle wrap.

A plan step may set a fade and plan.preview shows before and after; command.list describes the command; engine.capabilities lists features.clipFades; the renderer's read model, its fixture generator and the Node plan hasher accept the fields.

The app's split, duplicate (Ctrl+D) and Alt-drag copy carry a clip's fades in the same command.execute (clip.place takes no fade fields): split keeps the fade in on the left piece and moves the fade out to the right one (shortened to fit), a copy keeps both; a clip without fades gets no clip.set_fade (unit test edit-commands).
Crossfades and clip.set_mute, the rest of E-9, are not part of this feature. Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Engine: master gain in the document, with a command and a gesture target (E-11)
acceptance: The document holds the master gain in a singleton entity master ({schema: "siann.entity.master.v1", id: "master", gainMilliDb}, ref master:master; decided by the main session under the maintainer's delegation (Fable rule), 2026-11-15; architecture spec, siann-model), present only while the gain is not 0 dB and omitted from the canonical JSON when absent so existing hashes hold; the document stays siann.session_document.v2 (m5b-engine-buses-sends raises it later). The gain has the track entity's range and error (-144000..24000, -2147483648 minus infinity, invalid_gain), and a document that carries the entity with gainMilliDb 0 is rejected. A command master.set_gain {gainMilliDb} declares exactly {master:master}, is one undoable revision, reachable from plans and MCP, and announced by session.changed; master.set_gain 0 removes the entity, and plan.preview shows before: null for the 0 dB side (model and command tests: the range, the 0 dB removal, the document hash unchanged after a set and a set back to 0, undo, and a v2 document without the entity reading unchanged).

The master gain is a gesture target, {ref: master:master, param: gain} (protocol-gestures-v0.md; gain only, pan and mute on it are invalid_params, and its start value is 0 while the entity is absent): a fader gesture on it follows the lease rules of a track fader and commits one master.set_gain revision at its end.

The gain is applied after the sum of the tracks and before the master meter (meter key master; architecture spec, Master path), the click and device-side SRC; offline and realtime renders agree (null test), and a render at -6 dB is the 0 dB render scaled.
engine.capabilities lists features.masterGain; plan.preview shows before and after; a second connection sees the change. Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Engine: monitoring modes and the low-latency monitoring path (moved from M6b's m6b-monitoring)
acceptance: Monitoring per track is off, auto or input, set by a command track.set_monitor (one revision; omitted from the canonical JSON when off): input always passes the track's input through its strip to the output; auto passes it while stopped and while recording on an armed track and plays the track's clips otherwise; off never passes it.
Monitored input takes the low-latency path of the Latency model section, and engine.status reports the monitored round trip in frames.
The loopback offset test passes in every mode: a take recorded while monitoring lines up with the played impulse within one sample (fake device with a loopback).

Changing the mode during playback goes through the graph transition every structural change uses, with no discontinuity above the test's threshold and no allocation on the audio thread; engine.capabilities lists features.monitoring. Tour states changed: none (no UI).

features.title: Plan review in place: audition presentation, A/B on Shift+A, merge and discard (P2-3)
acceptance: While audition.changed reports that a branch is heard, the window has a 2 px violet frame, the banner under the top bar names the plan with Hear main, Merge and Discard, the branch chip shows the proposal's name, and the hearing switch in the right zone and in the status bar shows the side heard; all follow the event, also when another connection flips the side (e2e with a second client).

Shift+A flips the side heard (audition.hear) while a plan is auditioned and does nothing otherwise. Ctrl+Return with the right zone focused runs the selected plan's primary action (UI redesign 3.6), and the primary button then shows the key as the mockup's kbd does (unit test on the key table, e2e).

While the proposal is heard its ghosts are drawn solid from the branch snapshot (session.fetch at the branch revision that proposal.changed announces) and the values they replace as faint outlines; the snapshot is dropped on proposal.closed and on reconnect (unit test on the store, e2e on the crash scenario).
Structural edits (clip, track, marker and import commands, record) are disabled with a tooltip naming the reason while the proposal is heard; fader gestures still go to the side heard.

Merge sends proposal.merge and Discard sends proposal.discard; after either the frame, banner and ghosts are gone and the plan's card shows the new state. A partial approval auditions and merges only the ticked steps (e2e: 2 of 3 steps ticked; the merged revision holds exactly those two changes).

Their gate in app/test/fidelity/manifest.json (m5b-ui-audition) goes from pending to report in this pull request and the --hold-* tokens of these parts are deleted; nothing sets a gate to enforce. A side-by-side screenshot of the app and the mockup is attached for each state this feature changes, in en and zh-TW, with the fidelity report; the maintainer reviews it by eye, and no geometry or pixel result blocks.

features.title: Projects and audio setup: new, open, recent, save, the start view and the Studio Setup dialog
acceptance: New Project (Ctrl+N), Open (Ctrl+O), Save (Ctrl+S) and a list of the last ten bundles are commands of the key-command table and items of the application menu; the folder dialogs are the shell's (dialog.showOpenDialog and showSaveDialog behind the preload bridge, reached only from index.tsx), and in a plain browser tab New, Open and the recent list are absent: a command that needs the shell is rendered only when the preload bridge offers it, by the rule of UI redesign 3.0, while Save and Studio Setup need only the engine and stay. The application menu is Electron's native menu: this feature adds its File items (New, Open, Open Recent, Save) and Studio > Studio Setup, with labels from the renderer's catalogs and keys from the preset, shown as accelerators but not registered, so the renderer's dispatcher stays the one key layer; m5b-ui-keymap completes the other menus.

New creates a bundle with session.create and Open sends session.open; the window follows the session-opened event, drops the selection and view state of the old session and shows the new name in the title bar and the top bar. Opening a bundle another engine holds shows the lock refusal with the bundle's path.

The shell starts on the bundle opened last (remembered in user data, never in the session) and shows a start view with New, Open and the recent list when there is none or it is gone; SIANN_SESSION_DIR keeps working for tests.

Save sends session.save, and the window title and the top bar's session name mark revisions newer than the last save. The mark is the renderer's: its baseline is the head revision at the window's first sync, at every session.opened and the revision session.save answers, and it shows while the head differs from the baseline (a session reopened with journaled, unsaved revisions starts unmarked). Nothing is lost without it: every revision is journaled, so quitting needs no prompt (e2e: edit, quit without Save, relaunch, the edit is there).
e2e, the round trip of criterion B: New, add two tracks, place clips, change a gain, set locators, Save, quit, relaunch; the reopened session has the same document hash.

Studio Setup (Studio menu) lists engine.devices with their input and output channel counts, selects the output and the input device through engine.select_device, and shows sample rate, buffer size, input and output latency and whether device-side SRC is active from engine.status; a failed open shows the engine's code and Studio Setup then sends engine.select_device with the previous id and inputId, so the previous device is the selected one again (nothing is sent when no device ran); SRC is shown active when the device's sampleRate in engine.status differs from the session's. With no device, a click on a transport button disabled for that reason opens Studio Setup, and its tooltip names Studio Setup after the reason.
Every new string is in the three catalogs. Tour states changed: the title in the top bar of every state; appends 29 (start view) and 30 (Studio Setup).

features.title: Engine: position markers and cycle markers as document entities (E-8)
specRefs: siann-command (pure C++) — the core of SIANN
acceptance: A marker entity {id, number, name, position, length?} (audio-domain frames as decimal strings; a length makes it a cycle marker) with the commands marker.add, marker.move, marker.rename and marker.remove, each one revision, undoable, journaled, reachable from plans and MCP and announced by session.changed. Numbers are unique per kind and the lowest free one is assigned when omitted.

The document format version is raised with a migration that adds nothing: a literal bundle of the previous version opens with every recorded hash kept and is written in the new version at its next checkpoint.

plan.preview shows a marker with before and after; command.list describes the commands; engine.capabilities lists features.markers; the renderer's read model, its fixture generator and the Node plan hasher accept the entity type.

features.title: Engine: buses and sends in the document (moved from M6c's m6c-buses-sends)

features.title: Engine and protocol: requests from the user to a connected agent
acceptance: SIANN gains no agent runtime: a request is a message the engine hands to an agent that is already connected over MCP. agent.request {agentId, text, selection?: {tracks: [id], clips: [id]}} (the UI credential only; scope_denied for an MCP credential) queues the request for that agent and returns {request} (an arq_<hex> object, state pending); the engine stamps context {selection, locators (the head document's locators entity), cursor (the transport position as a decimal frame string, null without a transport port), headRevision} when it queues it. Selection ids are checked for the ID shape only (ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_-], 1 to 64), at most 256 per list, invalid_params otherwise; the context is data for the agent and is never executed. text is 1 to 4,000 characters, counted as Unicode code points after decoding well-formed UTF-8 (so at most 16,000 bytes); it follows the display-text rules of siann/model/display_text.hpp (no control character other than tab, LF and CR, no bidi formatting character, no U+2028/U+2029); otherwise invalid_request_text and nothing is queued (unlike plan title and intent, which are measured in bytes). agent_not_connected when the agent is unknown or not connected; at most 16 open requests (pending or taken) per agent, published as limits.agentRequestsPerAgent = 16: the 17th is agent_busy and nothing is queued.

The agent reads its queue through MCP tools in the propose scope (the UI token gets scope_denied): next_request {waitMs?} (agent.next_request) is a long poll that returns its oldest pending request and marks it taken; with none pending the command thread parks the call (it never blocks) and answers it when a request is queued for that agent, or with {request: null} once min(waitMs, limits.agentRequestWaitMs) has passed on ServerOptions::steadyClock; agentRequestWaitMs defaults to 25,000 and is always clamped below mcpRequestTimeout, which satisfies "at most 30 s". One parked call per agent: a second one answers the first with {request: null}. A parked call keeps its agent connected. A retry with the same JSON-RPC id returns the same request from the idempotency cache; an empty answer is not cached. An empty poll does not count as an action (no lastAction, no agent.changed), a delivering one does. answer_request (agent.answer_request) takes exactly one of {request, plan} (a plan it has submitted), {request, message} or {request, decline: true, message?} (invalid_params otherwise; message follows the text rule of item 1). plan.submit {..., request?} links the plan to the request, which then counts as answered; request is not hashed (like title and intent), is accepted only from the MCP credential whose agent is the request's addressee and only while the request is pending or taken (request_not_open otherwise; nothing is stored).

A request is pending, taken, answered, declined, cancelled (agent.cancel_request {request}, by the user) or expired: open requests expire when their agent disconnects (DELETE, or idle past agentIdleMs; a later reconnect does not revive them), when the agent is forgotten (agentsRetained), and when the served session changes (session.open, session.create), because their context names entities of the old session. Nothing is persisted; an engine restart drops every request (gate resolution). Every change publishes agent.request_changed {request}, and agent.requests {} gives a client that connects later the open requests (oldest first) and the last limits.agentRequestsClosedRetained = 16 closed ones.

A request changes nothing in the session: it is engine state, not a revision and not in the bundle, and the only way its outcome reaches the document is a plan that the user approves (test: an answered request leaves its plan awaiting approval, and the revision is unchanged).
The shape (method and tool names, whether the agent polls or waits, the bounds) is settled by the human gate agent-request-shape before implementation.

features.title: The Editor tab of the lower zone and the Channel zone
acceptance: The lower zone has an Editor tab beside MixConsole: the selected clip in a sample editor, its source's waveform with the clip's range marked, a ruler and its own horizontal zoom (G and H while the lower zone has the focus). A double-click on a clip's body or Return on a selected clip shows the lower zone on that tab (command editor.open); with no clip selected the tab says so, and with several selected it shows the primary one (the app's selectedClipId, the clip the info line reads). A double-click on a fade handle or inside a fade's shaded area keeps its m5b-ui-fades meaning (this feature depends on m5b-ui-fades and adds its double-click behind that one's hit test), and the volume control, the corner handles, the 4 px edges and the repeat handle do not open the editor. While the project zone itself has the focus and a clip is selected, Return is editor.open and does not enter the zone; with no clip selected it enters the zone as everywhere else (UI redesign 2.1 and 3.6).

Dragging an end of the range in the editor resizes the clip and the volume control sets its gain, with the commands, snap and modifiers of the event display: one revision each, restored by one undo. The editor draws on the two-layer surface from the peak pyramid and adds no protocol request.

The Channel zone button, the first of the four zone buttons, and Ctrl+Alt+C show and hide the Channel tab: one full MixConsole strip for the selected track beside the Inspector, 96 px by default, 80 to 160 px, collapsible, off by default, its size and state kept in siann.layout.v1. It is the strip component of the MixConsole, with the same controls, gestures and meter. With no track selected the zone is shown empty, without a placeholder; the strip in the zone does not carry data-part-item="strip", so the MixConsole's strip-N numbering (UI redesign 10.3) does not shift while the zone is open. The Channel zone is a zone of its own (UI redesign 2.1): it sits at the window's left edge, left of the Inspector, is shown and hidden independently of the left zone, has its own focus frame, comes first in the Tab and F6 order when shown, and its boundary with the Inspector is a divider like the others; it fits the existing three-column grid of the window (app/renderer/ui/layout.css does not change). When the window shrinks it gives way after the left zone, and under 1100 px it starts collapsed with it (UI redesign 2.3, 2.4).

Ctrl+Alt+Left and Ctrl+Alt+Right step through the tabs of the focused zone (UI redesign 2.1; this feature binds the chord, first used by the lower zone's two tabs), and the focus keys of 2.1 apply to the new tab and zone. The left zone's Editor tab (the second span of inspector-tabs, Cubase's editor Inspector) is not this feature's and is not in the usable release: its box stays empty through M5b (UI redesign 2.1; docs/harness/follow-ups.md), so the left zone has one tab and the chord does nothing there; this feature corrects the comment in app/src/renderer/shell/Inspector.tsx that gives the box to it.

A lit e carries the class on and aria-pressed="true"; the shared rules have no .msr.e.on and the mockup never draws e lit, so its look is an app-only rule .msr.e.on in shell.css on existing tokens (background --bg-5, colour --tx-1, border --tx-3); no shared rule and no token is added.
